$comment: First slice of the HITL escalation design (issue #1187, decision-tier rule
at #1187 comment 5800142871, Fable second opinion at #1187 comment
5800683025). `scripts/land-stack.mjs` reads this file to classify a pull
request's changed-file set into a tier, and to refuse to merge a tier-1 or
tier-2 pull request whose review evidence does not satisfy the rule below.
This is a merge-train gate, not a CI workflow: it costs no GitHub Actions
minutes, calls no model, and waits on nothing, matching AGENTS.md's
'Model-assisted code review is manually initiated' rule word for word --
see docs/HITL.md for why the record requirement lives here instead of in
verify-standards.yml.
TIER CLASSIFICATION IS A UNION-OVER-PATHS, MAX-OVER-TIERS OPERATION, OVER
ONE PULL REQUEST'S OWN DIFF. Every changed path in a pull request is
classified independently against tier2.globs, then tier1.globs minus
tier1RecordExempt.globs; the pull request's overall tier is the HIGHEST
tier any single path reaches. Spreading a change across many files never
lowers its tier below what one file alone would demand. KNOWN GAP
(#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 15): for a merge-train BATCH pull
request stacking several already-approved constituent PRs, only the
batch PR's own diff (against its own base) is classified today --
classifying the union of every constituent PR's own diff individually is
not implemented in this slice. In practice a batch PR's diff already
contains every constituent's changes relative to the batch's base, so
this still catches a tier-1/tier-2 path somewhere in the stack; what it
does NOT do is attribute a finding to which constituent PR introduced it,
or classify a constituent against ITS OWN base rather than the batch's.
Scaled back here rather than left overclaimed.
THIS FILE, AND THE REST OF THE ENFORCEMENT SURFACE IT DEFINES, ARE
TIER-2, NOT TIER-1 (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 13). A tier-1
change (two independent reviewers, neither the owner) could otherwise
narrow tier2.globs -- for example removing governance/model-
qualifications/** from it -- and downgrade the owner-only boundary
without the owner ever being involved. tier2.globs below therefore
names this file itself, scripts/land-stack.mjs and its test (the code
that reads and enforces it), docs/contracts/decision-record.json and
scripts/check-decision-records.mjs and its test (the decision-record
contract and validator the tier-2 gate also runs inline -- see
'RUN CHECK-DECISION-RECORDS INSIDE THE GATE' below), package-scope.json
(the publishing scope -- CLAUDE.md's own rule already treats it as the
one place that value lives), and scripts/lib/** (helper modules a
check:*.mjs or land-stack.mjs itself imports, previously a known,
acknowledged gap -- Fable's point 2 and #1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
should-fix 13 -- now closed by moving the whole directory to tier-2
rather than trying to name only the gate-relevant subset by hand).
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM governance/merge-policy.json: that file's
own $comment declares it 'THE ONE PLACE THIS REPOSITORY'S PERMITTED MERGE
METHODS ARE DECLARED' -- a narrowly scoped drift-alarm for GitHub's own
merge-method setting. Review-tier classification is a different policy
domain (what evidence a change needs, not which merge button is used), so
it gets its own file rather than widening merge-policy.json's declared
scope. scripts/land-stack.mjs reads both.
GOVERNANCE/DECISIONS/** IS TIER-1, NOT TIER-0 (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
blocking finding 4). An earlier version of this file exempted decision
records from every tier as 'a pure record file with its own rules' --
that made 'run check-decision-records inside the gate' (below) the ONLY
thing standing between an unreviewed pull request and a self-issued
'owner' decision record that then authorizes a real tier-2 change,
reviewed by nobody. Decision records are no longer exempt: adding or
changing one requires the same tier-1 independent-review bar as any
other governance path, on top of (not instead of) the shape validation
below.
RUN CHECK-DECISION-RECORDS INSIDE THE GATE (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
blocking findings 4 and 5). scripts/land-stack.mjs imports
`validateDecisionRecordShape` and `isRelaxationPastSunset` directly from
scripts/check-decision-records.mjs (not a re-implementation) and applies
them at two points: `evaluateChangedDecisionRecords` refuses ANY pull
request (any tier) that adds or edits a malformed governance/decisions/
*.json file, and `evaluateTier2Decision` refuses to treat a record as
tier-2 authority at all unless it is itself schema-valid, `tier: "tier-2"`
(a tier-1 record is never tier-2 authority), not superseded by a later
record, and not a relaxation past its own sunset -- and treats an
unparseable `expiry` as already expired, never as unexpired.
KNOWN GAPS REMAINING (see docs/HITL.md 'Honour-system limits' for the
full discussion): this classifies files named in the pull request's own
declared diff, paginated directly against the REST Pulls API (never
`gh pr view --json files`, which silently truncates past 100 entries --
#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, blocking finding 3) and cross-checked against
the pull request's own `changedFiles` count, refusing to classify at all
on a mismatch or an empty list. It still does not reach a `package.json`
`scripts` VALUE beyond the file itself being tier-1 -- a tier-1 reviewer
still has to actually read the diff of that file, the same as any other
tier-1 path; this file draws the path boundary, not the review quality.
BOOTSTRAP (#1187 review at df15ab87, should-fix 9): this file, once this
pull request adds it, does not exist on `main` until this very pull
request merges. Every pull request `scripts/land-stack.mjs` classifies
before that merge -- including the one that adds this file -- reads a
base ref where `governance/review-tiers.json` 404s, and
`defaultReadReviewTierConfig` throws rather than guessing a default.
That is fail-closed and correct, not a bug: it also means THIS pull
request cannot pass `land-stack.mjs --status` against itself, ever, by
construction -- there is no prior state where the config existed to
classify it against. It is also tier-2 (self-inclusion, above), so no
decision record could pre-authorize it either, for the same reason. The
first landing of this file is necessarily a plain, owner-approved
`gh pr merge`, the documented skip path (docs/HITL.md), not a gate this
conductor itself can clear. Every later change to this file goes through
the gate normally, once a prior version of it exists on `main` to read.
Ordinary gate and check scripts, CI workflow definitions, formal
contracts, governance policy (minus the record-shaped files carved out
below), and the handful of root documents that state this repository's
public safety and contribution rules. Matches the tier-1 path
description in #1187 comment 5800142871.
'gate and check scripts' is read as every scripts/check-*.mjs (and its
own .test.mjs), plus collect-review-evidence.mjs (the review-evidence
collector verify-standards.yml depends on) and the gate-suite runners
check:gates itself invokes. THE ENFORCEMENT SURFACE ITSELF --
land-stack.mjs, this file, the decision-record contract/validator, and
scripts/lib/** -- is tier-2, not tier-1; see this file's own header
comment for why.
Exactly the independence rule at #1187 comment 5800142871, tightened
by #1187 review at 8e6d97ea (blocking findings 1-2, should-fix 9):
- Exactly ONE current-head role:"author" record must exist. More than
one is ambiguous and refused outright -- never resolved to 'the
first one found', which would let a second author-role record
quietly count as an independent reviewer.
- ANY current-head independent reviewer record whose state is
'reject' or 'changes-requested' refuses the merge immediately and
is NEVER outvoted by a later approving pair from other reviewers --
'If they disagree, or either says reject, escalate to the owner
with both positions', and 'tier-1 reviewers disagree' is listed
under 'escalate immediately, whatever the tier'.
- Otherwise, a qualifying pair requires: state 'approved' on both
records ('commented' never counts -- the rule requires 'both
recommend acceptance'); one record 'primary' depth and the other
'secondary' depth (the rule's own 'a first reviewer plus a
stronger-model second opinion' pairing -- two 'primary' records do
not satisfy it); distinct instanceId from each other and from the
author; and differing model or provider.
Enforced by scripts/land-stack.mjs's evaluateTier1Independence against
structured `foundry-review-record` comments (docs/contracts/
review-record.json) at the pull request's EXACT current head -- a
record whose headSha does not match the live head is stale and
ignored, the same staleness discipline #1311 established for GitHub's
own native reviews. A record from a comment EDITED after it was
posted is dropped entirely, never trusted (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
should-fix 11).
'governance/ (minus pure record files, which have their own rules)'
(#1187 comment 5800142871). Every path below is committed evidence or
history -- appended to, or replaced wholesale by a script, never
hand-edited as policy -- and each already has its own gate (release
readiness, qualification-record-required, package-identity checks,
etc.) enforcing its shape. Requiring a second independent reviewer on
top of an existing automated gate for a pure record write would not
buy additional safety, only friction.
governance/decisions/** is DELIBERATELY NOT listed here (#1187 review
at 8e6d97ea, blocking finding 4) -- see this file's own header
comment. It is tier-1 like any other governance/** path, on top of
(not instead of) scripts/check-decision-records.mjs's own shape
validation, which land-stack.mjs runs inline regardless of tier.
governance/model-qualifications/ is intentionally NOT listed here --
it is promoted to tier-2 below instead of merely staying tier-1,
because every row in it requires per-model owner approval by design
(see docs/HITL.md and governance/model-qualifications/allowlist.json).
'define tier-2 globs for paths the owner reserves (rulesets or
settings-as-code, if any exist; propose them)' (task instruction).
Measured against this repository's own tree today (2026-09-23):
no branch-ruleset or repository-settings-as-code file exists IN this
git tree -- governance/merge-policy.json's own $comment says why:
'the merge methods a repository offers live in GitHub's own settings
store, not in the git tree, and writing them needs an
Administration-level credential no gate here holds.' The same is true
of the branch-protection ruleset scripts/land-stack.mjs itself reads
at merge time (gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}).
'.github/rulesets/**' is a PROPOSED, forward-declared glob: if this
repository ever gains a settings-as-code export of its branch
ruleset or repository settings (a real capability GitHub offers, not
adopted here yet), that path is tier-2 the moment it exists, with no
further decision needed to make it so. It matches no file today, so
it changes nothing about this pull request.
governance/model-qualifications/** IS real and matches today: the
model allowlist explicitly requires per-row owner approval
(approvedBy: "owner") before land-stack treats any record on it as
qualified for C3 (docs/HITL.md, governance/model-qualifications/
allowlist.json).
The remaining entries are the enforcement surface itself -- this file,
the conductor that reads it, the decision-record contract/validator,
the publishing scope, and gate helper modules -- added per #1187
review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 13; see this file's own header comment.
A path glob used to authorize a tier-2 change via a decision record's
own `links.paths` (not this file) must be EITHER a literal path with no
glob metacharacters, OR EXACTLY ONE of this section's own `globs`
entries, verbatim -- enforced by scripts/land-stack.mjs's
`isOverbroadPathGlob`, computed against this actual tier config, not a
fixed canary-path list (#1187 review at df15ab87, blocking finding 4:
the canary approach let `governance/**`, `.github/**`, `scripts/lib/**`
and a bare `*.yml` glob all pass as 'not overbroad', none of them
enumerable against a small fixed set; #1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
blocking finding 4 was the first pass at this rule).
Enforced by scripts/land-stack.mjs's evaluateTier2Decision: at least
one governance/decisions/*.json record that is itself schema-valid,
`tier: "tier-2"`, `status: "decided"`, `decidedBy: "owner"`, not
superseded, not a relaxation past its own sunset, with an `expiry`
that parses and is in the future (an unparseable expiry is treated
as already expired), and linked to this change either by
pull-request number (links.pullRequests) or by a non-overbroad path
glob covering every tier-2 path the pull request touches
(links.paths). See docs/contracts/decision-record.json.
